The article "The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Future of Work" by Sarah Miller explores the multifaceted ways Artificial Intelligence (AI) is poised to reshape the global labor market. This leads to the concept of **job augmentation**, where AI tools enhance human capabilities rather than replacing them entirely.

The article also delves into the **transformation of existing roles**. Miller suggests that many jobs will evolve, with AI becoming an integral part of daily workflows. For instance, doctors might use AI for diagnostics, lawyers for legal research, and teachers for personalized learning plans. This integration will require workers to adapt and acquire new digital literacy and AI-interaction skills.

Miller concludes by stressing the importance of **proactive measures** to navigate this transition successfully. She advocates for robust investment in lifelong learning, reskilling, and upskilling programs to equip the workforce with future-proof skills. Additionally, she calls for policymakers to consider new social safety nets and economic models to address potential income inequality and unemployment arising from widespread automation. Ultimately, Miller presents AI not as an inevitable destroyer of jobs, but as a powerful force whose impact on the future of work will largely depend on how societies choose to adapt and harness its potential.
